title: Focus publishes its first issue.
text: Focus is a German-language news magazine published by Hubert Burda Media. Established in 1993 as an alternative to the Der Spiegel weekly news magazine, its editorial staff has been headquartered in Germany's capital of Berlin since 2015.

title: A man hijacks Lufthansa Flight 592.
text: Lufthansa Flight 592 was a regularly scheduled passenger flight from Frankfurt, Germany, to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, that was hijacked on February 11, 1993. The Lufthansa-operated Airbus A310 was hijacked by Nebiu Zewolde Demeke, a 20-year-old Ethiopian man seeking asylum who forced the pilot to fly to New York City.

title: The 1993 World Horticultural Exposition begins in Stuttgart.
text: The Internationale Gartenbauausstellung 93 was held in Stuttgart, Germany. Recognised by the Bureau International des Expositions (BIE), the Expo ran from April 23, 1993, to October 17, 1993.

title: Solingen arson attack of 1993.
text: The Solingen arson attack was one of the most severe instances of racist violence in modern Germany. On the night of 28–29 May 1993, four young German men (ages 16–23) belonging to the far right skinhead scene, with neo-Nazi ties, set fire to the house of a large Turkish family in the city of Solingen, in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

title: June 25–27: The first annual Düsseldorfer Jazz-Rally is held.
text: Düsseldorfer Jazz-Rally is an annual jazz festival in Düsseldorf, Germany. This music festival began in 1993 on an early summer weekend and has continued to occur on the same weekend every year since.

title: Hamburg state election, 1993
text: The 1993 Hamburg state election was held on 19 September 1993 to elect the members of the 15th Hamburg Parliament. After the 1991 election, a group of CDU members brought a complaint over deficiencies in the party's nomination process to the Constitutional Court of Hamburg.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1993
text: Germany has been represented at every Eurovision Song Contest since its inaugural edition in 1956, except in 1996 when its entry did not qualify past the audio-only pre-selection round, and consequently did not enter the final and does not count as one of its 69 appearances. No other country has been represented as many times.

title: “More and More” by Captain Hollywood Project
text: "More and More" is a song by German Eurodance music project Captain Hollywood Project. It was released in July 1992 by the record labels Blow Up and Dino Music as the first single from their first album, Love Is Not Sex.

title: “Would I Lie to You?” by Charles & Eddie
text: "Would I Lie to You?" is a song by American soul music duo Charles & Eddie. Written by Mike Leeson and Peter Vale, and produced by Josh Deutsch, it was released in August 1992 by Capitol Records as the debut single from the duo's first album, Duophonic.

title: “I Will Always Love You” by 25 January
text: "I Will Always Love You" is a song written and originally recorded in 1973 by American singer-songwriter Dolly Parton. Written as a farewell to her business partner and mentor Porter Wagoner, expressing Parton's gratitude and also her decision to pursue a solo career, the country single was released in 1974.

title: “All That She Wants” by 8 March
text: "All That She Wants" is a song by the Swedish group Ace of Base. It was released in Scandinavia in August 1992, by Mega Records, as the second single from the group's debut studio album, Happy Nation, and in the following year, it was released as the first single from the 1993 album The Sign in North America.

title: “Informer” by 3 May
text: "Informer" is a song by Canadian reggae musician Snow, released in August 1992 by EastWest America and Motor Jam Records as the first single from his debut album, 12 Inches of Snow. The song is well known for the line "a licky boom boom down" and for Snow's fast toasting and often unintelligible lyrics.

title: “Mr. Vain” by 21 June
text: "Mr. Vain" is a song by German musical group Culture Beat, released in April 1993 by Dance Pool as the lead single from the group's second studio album, Serenity.

title: “What's Up” by 23 August
text: "What's Up?" is a song by American rock group 4 Non Blondes, released in March 1993 by Interscope Records as the second single from their debut album, Bigger, Better, Faster, More!.

title: “Go West” by 1 November
text: "Go West" is a song by American disco group Village People, released in June 1979 by Casablanca Records as the second single from their fourth studio album of the same name. The song was written by Jacques Morali, Henri Belolo and lead singer Victor Willis, while Morali produced it.

title: “I'd Do Anything for Love (But I Won't Do That)” by Meat Loaf
text: "I'd Do Anything for Love" is a song written by Jim Steinman and performed by American rock singer Meat Loaf with additional vocals by Lorraine Crosby. The song was released in August 1993 as the first single from the singer's sixth album, Bat Out of Hell II: Back into Hell (1993).
